long_biography.plain_text:
John Herting left school at 15 to join the engineering-supplies business run by his father, Fred. When Fred died in 1969, the 27-year-old son took responsibility for moving the firm forward. It developed into a national distributor of fixings, ironmongery and related products for housebuilders and contractors, supported by its own warehousing and delivery operation.

His second durable commitment was Brentford. After joining the board in 1992, Herting provided sponsorship, invested personally and helped the club through financially difficult years. He later supported the transition to supporter and then Matthew Benham control, retiring as a director after 21 years while remaining an associate director and advertiser.
